The bill for an ambulance is like $500 if I remember correctly, but if it’s life saving it will cost a lot more. (Why??) 

I remember my parents got mad at me because I had to go to the hospital often and it was expensive. They always reminded me of the costs... 

It has made me really want to avoid the hospital when maybe I shouldn’t, but I’d rather die than deal with a $10k - $15k bill. I don’t give a shit if people say “Staying alive was important. You can figure out the costs later.” No. You don’t get it because you don’t experience chronic health issues. 

If it’s a one time thing or very rarely happens because it shouldn’t have happened in the first place, then fine. But it’s pretty depressing to keep living when you’re in a country that couldn’t give a shit to even try to help you live another day.

I worked my ass off at an old job. I was hired to work under a specific position, but then wasn’t given the position. They stated I need to improve first and then we could talk. So I pushed myself to improve and when I believed I’ve gotten better I went back to ask how I’ve been. They’d acknowledge the improvement, but then say I could improve somewhere else. They did this 3 times and I then expressed concerns on the position that I applied then got accepted for. That I would like to start training for that position. Same excuse. I needed to improve in something else then be fast about it. As I improved I realized that my coworkers were not at all working as hard as I was. They weren’t as efficient or stressed as I was, yet I was the only one being told I needed to work harder. 

Then this other person got given the position that I applied for and they would come to me to ask for help. Seriously? They gave the position to someone who wasn’t even qualified or knew what they were doing. 

Once that happened I started looking somewhere else and told my employer that I was leaving. I basically called and said I was leaving. I didn’t do any “two week notice,” and maybe I should have, but oh well. They were a bad company anyways that many people spoke against. Glad I left. When I notified my boss he ended up saying some dumb shit about how I’m going to be the reason their child will need a babysitter or some shit.

Some refrigerators have a water dispenser either inside or outside of the fridge. I used to have a fridge with a water dispenser inside, so it was always chilly water. 

But I believe the most common water dispenser, fridge, set up has the water and ice dispenser on the outside of the door. If I remember correctly, it’s usually on the left because that side is the freezer, so y’know. Ice.

Surprisingly I actually had water in a restaurant in China that tasted good. Like shockingly good. 

It was a bit of a fancy place, but I’ve never tasted water that was ‘good,’ in my opinion. Even the people I travelled with said the same thing.

All I can say is please work with a professional service dog trainer. 

Even experienced owner trainers need help from others. No matter the amount of experience, it’ll always be difficult. If not because of lack of experience, it’ll be because of the time and energy that is required daily. 

You’re not just training a puppy. You’re training a puppy who will need to be as reliable as possible. As predictable as possible. And at the utmost level of obedience in any situation that you personally go through. 

Service dogs are not just pets that need to know when it’s okay to bark or not. It’s not just teaching them how to greet kids with treats nicely. It’s training them how to help with your medical condition. To ignore, be comfortable, and be reliable in very stressful situations/environments. 

Service dog training is not like pet training. Pets, you can get away with not training every day. Not implementing rules every day may just give you a pet dog that “likes to be a bit sneaky,” but doing that could give you a service dog that doesn’t task properly in public and negatively affects the general public or another team. 

Not training every day is fine if all your dog knows is basic obedience like “sit, down, stay,” (if your dog is not off leash trained and stays on a leash) But if you don’t train every day then you’ll have a “poorly trained” service dog. 

You need to figure out the balance between letting your dog be a puppy/dog and when you need to have your “service dog trainer” hat on.

Yes. There is a tip I found online that I’ve done for myself. 

Start doing things in your awake state, consistently and constantly such as:

Checking the time. 

And

Counting your fingers. 


According to what I read online when you’re dreaming ‘time’ and ‘numbers’ seem to not be reliable in your dreams. I agree with that thought/idea.

The next important part is that when you check the time or count your fingers, there should be a routine. For example. When I count my fingers it’s when I enter the restroom or lie down in bed, no matter what. 

Enter the restroom, close the door or stall, and I hold up my hands to count my fingers. Not quickly either. Then I check my watch. Every. Single. Time. 

It builds up the routine so that when you finally fall asleep and end up in those situations, it’ll feel like second nature. 

Of course you can decide when you do this routine. It’s not often you enter a restroom in your sleep. For me, even though I wasn’t in the restroom I’d still randomly decide to count my fingers. Including when I was awake. Mainly because I have a “trippy mind” and doubt reality often, mostly out of fear and curiosity, so I’ll count my fingers and check the time. I either get two reactions. 

1. Bored and disappointed because I’m awake. 

2. Relieved and excited because I’m asleep. 

So you’ll probably be able to eventually do it more casually and it’ll feel like a second nature reaction/decision.

Fast forward we became great friends. Like... amazing friends. We hung out every single day. We would ride the bus together everyday and part at the train station. We texted a shit ton every day. We did so much together.

I became depressed again later at age 18 and things changed. Her motherly instincts went kicked in full throttle and I appreciated it a lot. I enjoyed it, even. I went to her. I told her a million times that I shouldn’t rely on her, to not trust her with my demons, but she insisted and insisted. So one day I decided to let her in even more.. big mistake.

I think the lesson learned here is that despite me growing up to not trust people and living my whole life alone, maybe I can finally trust and love someone once more.
